lessons.title: Spawning items and the left panel
lessons.summary: Open a category, tap an item tile, and watch it drop into the field.
lessons.intro: Everything you build starts in the panel on the left of the screen. This lesson shows how to find an item and put it in the field.

steps.title: Pick a category
text: Along the top of the left panel there is a row of small icons. The first one is a swap arrows button, the others are categories. The game shows icons only, with no names.
When you tap a category, the header under the icons changes (for example MECHANICS) and the item tiles change with it.
tips: The row of icons scrolls sideways. In the recordings the set of icons was not always the same, so the one you want may be off to the side.
unknown: Which icon is which category is only known from the section header that appears after you tap it. We could not name every icon.

steps.title: Tap a tile to spawn the item
text: Items are shown as a grid of three tiles per row, each with its name underneath. Tap a tile once and the item appears in the field.
It is created above the ground and falls under gravity, so it lands and may tumble. Leave room for it to fall.
tips: Ragdolls and loose items can be dragged with a finger once they are in the field. Objects stay attached to ropes while you drag them.
unknown: The recordings do not show how the game chooses where the item appears. In some clips a see-through copy showed first, then turned solid.

steps.title: Hide the panel and bring it back
text: The arrow at the top-left edge of the panel hides it, which gives you the whole field. When it is hidden, a grid icon appears in the top-left corner. Tap it to show the panel again.
At the bottom of the panel, CLEAR EVERYTHING removes all items and CLEAR LIVING removes ragdolls. After a ragdoll dies, the second button changes to CLEAR CORPSES.
tips: Hide the panel before you take a good look at a build. It is also in the way when you want to tap objects on the left side.

steps.title: Where things are
text: These are the sections we saw in the recordings, with a few example items. Section names are shown as headers in the panel.
facts: Melon, Pumpkin, Corn, Apple, Cactus, Tomato
Pistol, Auto Pistol, Revolver, Machine Gun, Minigun
Fougasse, C4, Land Mine, Nuclear Bomb
Freeze Grenade, Explosive Charge, Bouncy Bomb Box
Gyroscope, Motorized Wheel, Rocket Engine, Piston, Conveyor, Door
Jeep, APC, Scooter, Bicycle, Car Seat, Jetpack
Brick Wall, Brick, Short Beam, Wooden Plank
Crate, Barrel, Table, Chair, Weight, Wheel
tips: Only items we measured can be placed on this site's Build page. Find sizes in the Wiki.

lessons.title: Tapping an object: the menu
lessons.summary: What each button in the 3 by 3 menu is called, what it does, and which ones we have not identified yet.
lessons.intro: Tap any object in the field and a menu opens. The same menu is where you change parameters, freeze things and delete them.

steps.title: Open the menu
text: Tap an object. A square menu with nine cells opens, with a small X at the corner to close it.
tips: Some objects get extra or fewer cells. A Helicopter menu had no DEBUG OUTPUTS, for example.

steps.title: The six labelled buttons
text: Page 1 has six buttons with text under their icons: EDIT PARAMETERS, DEBUG OUTPUTS, DELETE, FREEZE, DISABLE COLLISIONS and ACTIVATE.

EDIT PARAMETERS opens the settings panel (lesson 3). DELETE removes the object. FREEZE holds it in place and turns into UNFREEZE once the object is frozen. ACTIVATE seems to do the same as the power button (inferred).
unknown: DEBUG OUTPUTS opens a small window, but its content was never captured.
DISABLE COLLISIONS: we only know its name.

steps.title: The three buttons with no label
text: The last row has three icons and no text: a power symbol, a tripod (or axes) symbol and overlapping squares. In some menus an eye icon was also seen.
unknown: We have not seen what any of these three do. The plans on this site never use them.

steps.title: Page 2 of the menu
text: The menu has a second page with seven buttons: COPY, FLIP, DISABLE DAMAGE, RESIZE, FREEZE ROTATION, INVISIBLE and NON-DRAGGABLE.
The step guides on this site tell you to use FLIP when a part should face the other way.
unknown: The recordings show the second page but not how the game switches to it. Look for a small arrow or try swiping the menu.
Only the names are known for DISABLE DAMAGE, RESIZE, FREEZE ROTATION, INVISIBLE and NON-DRAGGABLE. We never saw the resize controls.

steps.title: Extra buttons on some objects
text: Vehicles add START DRIVING and DROP PASSENGERS to the menu. The Contraption Spawner adds SELECT SAVE FILE, which opens a searchable list of your saved contraptions with SELECT and CANCEL buttons. The power button then spawns the chosen save.
tips: A Contraption Spawner menu in the recordings showed UNFREEZE instead of FREEZE, because that spawner was already frozen (inferred).

lessons.title: Parameters: EDIT PARAMETERS
lessons.summary: Open the settings panel, type numbers, tick boxes, and see the values we have recorded for real items.
lessons.intro: Many mechanical items have settings. You change them in a small panel that attaches to the object.

steps.title: Open the panel
text: Tap the object, then tap EDIT PARAMETERS. A panel opens on the side of the screen. A thin white line joins it to the object it belongs to.
Here the example is a Rocket Engine, which only has one setting: FORCE 600.

steps.title: Numbers and checkboxes
text: Number boxes open the Android keyboard. Type the number and tap OK. Yes/no settings are checkboxes.
The Directional Accelerator shows both kinds: FORCE 600 and ANGLE 0 are numbers, GLOBAL ANGLE was ticked and FREEZE ROTATION was not.
unknown: The game never showed minimum or maximum values, or units. We do not know what range is safe.

steps.title: A conveyor example
text: The Conveyor has SPEED, REVERSED and LENGTH. In the recording it started at SPEED 10, REVERSED unchecked, LENGTH 1. Then the owner ticked REVERSED, set LENGTH 2 (the belt became about twice as long) and set SPEED 20.
tips: If a belt carries things the wrong way, tick REVERSED.

steps.title: Explosive Charge
text: The Explosive Charge has the longest list we saw. The panel scrolls. Only the first five rows are drawn here; the last two are LOOP TIME STEP 1 and DELAY 3.
unknown: With DELAY 3, the blast came roughly 2 to 3 seconds after the power button was pressed. That is a guess from video frames.

steps.title: Every value we have seen
text: These are the values that were on screen in the recordings. They are not recommendations.

head: Item
Parameters shown
rows: FORCE 600, ANGLE 0, GLOBAL ANGLE checked, FREEZE ROTATION unchecked
RADIUS 5, POWER 2, DAMAGE 80, TEMPERATURE 5, DESTROYABLE unchecked, LOOP TIME STEP 1, DELAY 3
COLOR (hue wheel, brightness slider, hex box)

lessons.title: Ropes, rods, cables and chains
lessons.summary: The two-tap flow for joining two objects, and how the different link tools behave.
lessons.intro: Joining things together is how you make swings, towers, carts and bridges. All the line tools work the same way: pick the tool, tap point A, tap point B.

steps.title: Open the tool picker
text: The button at the bottom-right opens the tool picker. It shows icons only, in a grid that scrolls sideways. Tap an icon to pick it. The picker closes and the button now shows your tool.

steps.title: Tap point A, then point B
text: Tap the first object at the spot where the rope should be fixed. A ring marks your first tap and the text SELECT THE SECOND ROPE POINT appears. Tap the second object. The link is drawn between the two spots you tapped.
tips: The point you tap matters. The link is fixed to that exact spot, not to the middle of the object.
Plans on this site can store these anchor points, and the step guide tells you where to tap.

steps.title: How the tools differ
text: Names are not shown on screen, so these are descriptions of the icons plus what each one did in the recordings.

head: Icon
What it did
rows: Thin rope. Sags when slack and pulls the objects together.
Behaves like the rope: flexible, sags.
Straight and rigid. The objects swung around it at a fixed distance.
Stays fairly tight while the objects tumbled.
Stretched to about three times the original gap when a crate was thrown (elastic or adjustable, inferred).
Moves liquid between two containers by itself.

unknown: Not tried in the recordings: the + tool, the checker block, the tan square and the brown peg object.

steps.title: Try a rigid rod
text: Pick the thin grey rod from the same page and tap two points. The rod stays straight, so the two crates keep their distance when you push them.

lessons.title: Wires and the SELECT INPUT/OUTPUT window
lessons.summary: Use the rainbow-arrow tool to send an output from one object to an input on another.
lessons.intro: A wire lets one object trigger or control another. It is the game's way of connecting things without a chip.

steps.title: Pick the wire tool
text: Open the tool picker and choose the arrow with the rainbow line underneath. It is on the first page.

steps.title: Tap two objects
text: Tap the object that sends the signal first, then tap the object that receives it. The same SELECT THE SECOND ROPE POINT prompt appears. After the second tap, the SELECT INPUT/OUTPUT window opens.

steps.title: Choose OUTPUT and INPUT
text: The window has two columns. OUTPUT lists what the first object can send. INPUT lists what the second object can receive.
ACTIVATION was seen in both columns. ANGLE was seen as an OUTPUT of one object. COLOR was seen as an INPUT, for lamps. A line at the bottom shows your pair, for example ACTIVATION / ACTIVATION.
unknown: The list changes with the objects. We only saw these three names. We do not know what ANGLE sends.

steps.title: Apply
text: Tap APPLY to make the wire. CLOSE leaves without making one. A crossed-eye icon sits next to the pair line; it is probably the switch for hiding the wire (inferred).
tips: Wires are real lines with physics. In the recordings a wire swung with the object it was attached to.
Triggering the first object lit the second object.

steps.title: What we still do not know
text: The chip editor and its ports were never shown, so this site does not plan chip circuits.
unknown: How a Chip connects to other objects.
Which objects offer which OUTPUT and INPUT names.
What the wire's DEBUG OUTPUTS menu lists.

lessons.title: Electricity: Generator, wire and Tesla Coil
lessons.summary: Join a Generator to other things with the lightning-bolt wire and press a power button.
lessons.intro: In the recordings, a Generator, a wire and a power button made sparks run through a ragdoll and made a Tesla Coil shoot arcs.

steps.title: Pick the electric wire
text: Open the tool picker, scroll to the second page, and pick the lightning bolt over a wooden bar. The name 'electric wire' is our guess from what it did.

steps.title: Tap the Generator, then the target
text: The flow is the same as for ropes. Tap the Generator, read SELECT THE SECOND ROPE POINT, then tap the second object. Power buttons appear at the bottom corners.

steps.title: Press the power button
text: Press a power button. The Tesla Coil shot purple-white arcs. A ragdoll joined to the Generator by a second wire showed white sparks along its body.
unknown: It was not clear which wire carried the power to the coil. In the recording a small black device sat in the chain.

steps.title: VOLTAGE and ACTIVATION VOLTAGE
text: Two electric settings were seen. VOLTAGE showed 10 and was later changed to 1000. A small black device had ACTIVATION VOLTAGE 10.
Open them with EDIT PARAMETERS like any other setting.
unknown: We are not sure which object the VOLTAGE panel belonged to. The catalog on this site lists it on the Generator, marked as uncertain.
Wiring for Battery, Adapter, Relay, Transformer and Voltmeter was never shown.

steps.title: Other powered things we saw
text: Fluorescent Lamp 1 and 2 lit up when a power button was pressed. The Defibrillator has two paddles on cables. Drag the paddles onto the torso of a ragdoll, press the power button and white sparks flash.

links.label: See the Generator, wire and Tesla Coil plan

lessons.title: Power buttons and activating things
lessons.summary: Where the power buttons are, what they trigger, and the pause, slow-motion and undo buttons.
lessons.intro: Engines, pistons and explosives do nothing until you activate them. Power buttons are how you do that.

steps.title: Find the power buttons
text: When an activatable object is in the field, two round power buttons appear: one at the bottom-left of the screen and one at the bottom-right.

steps.title: Tap one
text: Tapping a power button triggers the object. A Piston extends its rod and retracts it afterwards (SPEED 1 in the recording).
unknown: With several activatable objects in the field, we are not sure whether one button fires all of them. The recordings show two buttons for one item and two for several.

steps.title: ACTIVATE in the menu
text: The menu of an object has an ACTIVATE button. It most likely does the same thing for that object alone (inferred).

steps.title: Undo, slow motion and pause
text: The three buttons at the top-right are undo, slow motion and pause. While paused, the pause symbol turns into a play triangle. Use pause while you set things up, and slow motion to watch fast things.

steps.title: Things we saw being activated
text: These all reacted to a power button or to ACTIVATE in the recordings.
facts: spins; a crate it sat on tumbled

lessons.title: Reading sizes: crates and grid cells
lessons.summary: How to read the sizes on this site, why the Crate is the ruler, and how accurate they are.
lessons.intro: The game never shows sizes or mass. We measured items from screenshots and describe every size in crates.

steps.title: The Crate is the ruler
text: One crate is the size of the game's Crate. A Table is about 1.87 crates wide and 0.94 crates tall. Everything on this site is drawn to that scale, so two items side by side on the Build page really are in proportion.
tips: The grid in the player shows the same cells that the Build page uses.

steps.title: A grid cell is one eighth of a crate
text: The faint grid is divided into cells of 1/8 crate (0.125). Eight cells make a crate. The Pumpkin ragdoll is about 2.05 crates tall, or 16 cells.
Plans and guides quote both numbers, for example '0.22 crate (2 grid cells)'.

steps.title: How accurate are the sizes?
text: Sizes come from screenshots and are accurate to about two pixels. For big items that is under one percent. For the tiniest items it can be around eight percent, so treat them as close, not exact.
Items flagged 'edge unsure' on their Wiki page have a less certain size.
unknown: Mass was never shown for any item.

steps.title: Where to look
text: Every measured item has a page in the Wiki with its size in crates and cells. The Build page uses the same sizes.

lessons.title: Using the Build page and Base64 codes
lessons.summary: Plan on a true-to-scale grid, follow the generated step guide, and share a plan as a text code.
lessons.intro: The Build page is where you design a contraption before you touch the game. The result is a step guide that tells you what to tap.

steps.title: Plan on the grid
text: Open the Build page and add items from the list. They are placed on a grid at true scale, so you can see whether things fit, stack or overlap before you build in the game.

steps.title: Follow the step guide
text: Every plan becomes a list of steps. Each step names the item, says which section to open in the game, tells you where to put it (on the floor, on top of another item, how far from another one) and lists parameters to type. Link steps tell you where to tap for point A and point B.
tips: Parts that float in a plan come with a tip to FREEZE them (see the last lesson).
The guide only uses buttons we have seen in the recordings.

steps.title: Share a plan as a code
text: On the Build page, tap Export. A window shows your whole plan as one block of text, with buttons to copy it or download it as a .txt file. The text starts with MSB1: and the rest is Base64, which is just your plan written as letters and numbers.
To open a plan from a code, tap Import, paste the code (or choose the saved file) and tap Import again. It opens as a new copy, so nothing you already have is changed. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
tips: Copy every character. If the code is cut off, the import tells you so.
Plans save themselves in this browser only. Export a code to back them up or to move them to another device.

steps.title: Start from a premade plan
text: The Plans page has ready-made layouts that open straight in the Build page. They are untested in the game. Treat them as a starting point.

lessons.title: Freezing and keeping things in place
lessons.summary: Use FREEZE to hold parts in the air while you build, and UNFREEZE to let them go.
lessons.intro: Things fall as soon as they exist. FREEZE is the way to keep a part exactly where you put it.

steps.title: Freeze an object
text: Tap the object, then tap FREEZE. It stays where it is, even with nothing under it.

steps.title: Unfreeze it
text: Open the menu again. The button now says UNFREEZE. Tap it and gravity takes over.

steps.title: Why plans tell you to freeze
text: If a part in a plan is not resting on anything, the step guide adds a tip to FREEZE it. Otherwise it would fall as soon as you place it.
You can also pause the game with the pause button at the top-right while you set things up (inferred as a helpful habit; the recordings show the pause button but not this use).

steps.title: Related buttons
text: On page 2 of the menu there is a FREEZE ROTATION button. The Directional Accelerator also has a FREEZE ROTATION checkbox among its parameters. Only the names were seen, so we do not know exactly how they differ from FREEZE.
unknown: What FREEZE ROTATION does on its own, and whether NON-DRAGGABLE holds an object against your finger.
